alt: What are you putting off today? Just the word. Nobody else sees your reply. I’ll go first: the dentist. Every year.
Everything you dreaded this year. How much of it actually happened? A  most of it / B  hardly any Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.
If you said B, the data agrees. People with anxiety logged their worries for weeks. 91% never came true. LaFreniere & Newman, Behavior Therapy, 2020. Small study, 29 people.
99 kind comments. 1 mean one. Which one are you still thinking about at bedtime? Reply “the 1” or “the 99”. Answer tomorrow at 9.
The 1. You’re normal. Psychologists call it “bad is stronger than good”: one sting outweighs a lot of kindness. Baumeister et al., Review of General Psychology, 2001.
The friend you’ve texted most this month. Are you more like them than a year ago? Reply yes or no. Or send this to them and ask.
Aristotle would say yes. He thought good friends improve each other just by spending time together. Moodius paraphrase of Nicomachean Ethics, Book IX.
A student tells Confucius: “I’ve mastered kindness.” What does Confucius say? A  “Well done.” / B  “Not yet.” Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.
B. Brutal. Weirdly hopeful. “Ts’ze, you have not attained to that.” Analects V.11, tr. James Legge.
Who’s happier walking home? A  the friend who paid / B  the friend who didn’t Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.
Maybe A. In 120 of 136 countries, people who’d spent on others lately reported more wellbeing. Aknin et al., 2013. Linked, not proven to cause it.
A Roman emperor’s fix for a bad mood. A  wine / B  a list of his friends’ best bits Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.
B. Very wholesome. Slightly annoying. Marcus Aurelius thought about the good qualities of the people around him. Meditations 6.48.
A medical book in Timbuktu names a tree. Where can you see one today? A  a park in Mali / B  nobody knows which tree it is Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.
B. Still a mystery. Scholars still can’t identify some trees named in Timbuktu’s handbooks. History, not medical advice.
How long did Li Shizhen spend writing one book of medicines? A  2 years / B  27 years Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.
27 years. UNESCO now lists his Bencao Gangmu as world heritage. Your unfinished project has time. UNESCO Silk Roads. History, not medical advice.
Something a friend did this year that you never thanked them for. Reply with one word. Then go and thank them. I’ll check tomorrow. Gently.

Sent the thank-you? Reply “done”. In one study, writing and delivering a thank-you letter gave the biggest happiness boost of five exercises. It faded after a month, so repeat. Seligman et al., American Psychologist, 2005.
Egypt’s Ebers Papyrus, c. 1550 BCE, one of the oldest medical books. Where is it kept today? A  Cairo / B  Leipzig Reply with A or B. Answer tomorrow at 9.
B. Leipzig, Germany. Around 700 remedies, 3,500 years old, living in a university library. It has seen things. Encyclopaedia Britannica. History, not medical advice.
Two weeks of stories. Which do you want more of? A  forgotten history / B  how your mind works / C  being kind, with evidence Reply A, B or C. Most replies wins next week.
